scenario.summary: ARTEX is a Go-based autonomous AI penetration testing framework used by threat actors like Storm-0940 and Salt Typhoon to automate reconnaissance, web exploitation, and lateral movement. The framework coordinates multiple LLM agents to execute off-the-shelf tools at machine speed, progressing from initial access to cloud privilege escalation and mass data exfiltration in minutes.

hunt.name: ARTEX AI-Driven Perimeter Recon and Identity Probing
hunt.description: This hunt identifies the early autonomous phases of an ARTEX intrusion. Threat actors like Storm-0940 use the framework to automate reconnaissance and initial access, often moving from a credential spray to web application probing in minutes. We start by scoping the web server estate and identifying high-volume authentication failures that serve as a cheap lead. A gated agent then decides whether to trigger expensive queries into web application probing and the execution of worker tools like sqlmap or hydra. The hunt concludes with a triage agent correlating external identity pressure with internal behavioral artifacts to confirm the presence of an autonomous penetration testing agent.

config.scoping_notes: The hunt focuses on the internet-facing web server estate (Apache, Nginx, IIS) and the identity provider logs (Entra ID, Okta). High-velocity sprays against M365 or SaaS providers are the primary entry point.
config.beyond_detection: A standard rule might detect an individual tool like sqlmap. This hunt identifies the machine-speed agentic pattern—the rapid correlation of identity sprays with specific web probing across multiple surfaces—that distinguishes ARTEX from disparate automated scans.

config.content: SELECT DISTINCT device_hostname FROM hb_software_inventory WHERE LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%apache%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%nginx%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%sharepoint%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%screenconnect%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%httpd%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%iis%'
config.description: Identify hosts running web server software that are likely targets for autonomous scanning.
config.expected_signal: A list of hosts running common web services. This scopes follow-on queries to the internet-facing estate.

primitive_config.label: Scope potential web server targets
primitive_config.content: SELECT DISTINCT device_hostname FROM hb_software_inventory WHERE LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%apache%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%nginx%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%sharepoint%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%screenconnect%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%httpd%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%iis%'
primitive_config.expected: A list of hosts running common web services. This scopes follow-on queries to the internet-facing estate.

config.content: SELECT src_endpoint_ip, COUNT(*) AS attempt_count, COUNT(DISTINCT actor_user_name) AS unique_users, MIN(time) AS first_attempt, MAX(time) AS last_attempt FROM hb_auth_signin WHERE status_id = 2 AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY src_endpoint_ip HAVING attempt_count >= {{auth_failure_threshold}} ORDER BY attempt_count DESC
config.description: Identify source IPs exhibiting machine-speed authentication failure patterns consistent with AI-driven sprays.
config.expected_signal: A single IP address attempting dozens or hundreds of logins across multiple accounts in a narrow window. This is the durable behavioral lead for ARTEX.

primitive_config.label: High-volume identity pressure lead
primitive_config.content: SELECT src_endpoint_ip, COUNT(*) AS attempt_count, COUNT(DISTINCT actor_user_name) AS unique_users, MIN(time) AS first_attempt, MAX(time) AS last_attempt FROM hb_auth_signin WHERE status_id = 2 AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY src_endpoint_ip HAVING attempt_count >= {{auth_failure_threshold}} ORDER BY attempt_count DESC
primitive_config.expected: A single IP address attempting dozens or hundreds of logins across multiple accounts in a narrow window. This is the durable behavioral lead for ARTEX.

config.objective: Decide if the authentication failure counts and account diversity from the lead indicate an automated ARTEX-like agent.
config.description: Determine if the identity spray pattern is likely an automated agent that warrants further investigation of web logs.
config.expected_signal: A verdict confirming the automation level of the source IP.
config.success_criteria: A verdict on whether to proceed with the full investigation based on the spray intensity.

config.question: the evaluate-lead-agent verdict is malicious or suspicious for at least one source IP
config.condition: the evaluate-lead-agent verdict is malicious or suspicious for at least one source IP
config.description: Avoid expensive parallel queries if the initial spray does not show evidence of machine-speed automation.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, src_endpoint_ip, url_path, status_code, COUNT(*) AS request_count, MIN(time) AS first_request FROM hb_http_activity WHERE (('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0)) AND (instr(',' || '{{web_config_paths}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(url_path) || ',') > 0 OR url_path LIKE '%.env%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY device_hostname, src_endpoint_ip, url_path, status_code ORDER BY request_count DESC
config.description: Identify high-velocity HTTP requests for sensitive configuration files from the suspect IPs.
config.expected_signal: Bursts of requests for .env, web.config, or my.cnf files targeting the scoped web assets. Silence confirms these IPs did not probe these specific paths.

primitive_config.label: Sensitive configuration file probing
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, src_endpoint_ip, url_path, status_code, COUNT(*) AS request_count, MIN(time) AS first_request FROM hb_http_activity WHERE (('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0)) AND (instr(',' || '{{web_config_paths}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(url_path) || ',') > 0 OR url_path LIKE '%.env%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY device_hostname, src_endpoint_ip, url_path, status_code ORDER BY request_count DESC
primitive_config.expected: Bursts of requests for .env, web.config, or my.cnf files targeting the scoped web assets. Silence confirms these IPs did not probe these specific paths.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, process_cmd_line, user_name, time FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0)) AND (instr(',' || '{{offensive_tool_names}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(process_name) || ',') > 0 OR instr(',' || '{{offensive_tool_names}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(process_original_file_name) || ',') > 0 OR process_cmd_line LIKE '%sqlmap%' OR process_cmd_line LIKE '%hydra%' OR process_cmd_line LIKE '%ncrack%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Identify the execution of ARTEX's integrated worker tools on systems in the scoped estate.
config.expected_signal: Process execution for tools like nmap, hydra, or sqlmap. Silence proves these specific binaries did not run in the examined window.
